TESTIMONY OF BOB NEAL, NEW SHARON SELECTMAN
Good morning, Senators and Representatives:
My name is Bob Neal and for the past 32 days I have been on the New Sharon Select Board. I
am here today because the two selectwomen are at work and out of state. That leaves this job up
to the new kid on the block.
The New Sharon Select Board fully supports the full town assuming responsibility for the finances and operation of the New Sharon Water District. Consolidators always promise to
reduce costs. They don't always do it. But it appears the town could save as much as $13,000 a
year by taking on the billing of the 100 or so customers of the water district. That's $130 for each
water customer.
In the view of the select board, town taking responsible for the water system since the water district plays a vital role for the town in providing water to fire hydrants in the village and for several hundred yards along some roads. The district appears to have worked through its worst
financial problems, so this may be the opportune for the town and the district to combine eiiforts.
The town might well be able to help the water system upgrade and update. I was on the select board when our fire company became a town department, and I can see the result now in better
equipment, better training and better service. If we repeat with the water district our experience
with the fire company, everyone in town, whether or not a water customer, should benefit.
I will defer to Ed Fereira and Mark Deden for answering questions because, as I said, I am only
32 days into the job and still have a lot to learn.
Thank you for your attention.

Testimony of the Maine Public Utilities Commission
In Support of
LD 1346, An Act Regarding the Supply of Water to the Town of New Sharon
April 16, 2025
Senator Lawrence, Representative Sachs, and Distinguished Members of the Joint Standing Committee
on Energy, Utilities, and Technology (Committee), my name is Deirdre Schneider, testifying in support of LD 1346, An Act Regarding the Supply of Water to the Town of New Sharon on behalf of the Public
Utilities Commission (Commission).
LD 1346 repeals the charter of the New Sharon Water District and directs the Town of New Sharon to
assume operations, the assets and liabilities of the District.
In September 2023, the Commission opened a fonnal investigation to examine the acts and practices of the District, as the District appeared to have potential difficulties in satisfying its financial obligations. The Commission expanded the scope of the investigation to include consideration of and the appointment of a receiver for the District because the district was also having issues with maintaining a
quorum to conduct the District's business. A January 18, 2024, order appointed a receiver to oversee
the operations of the District. By February 14, 2024, the Town had appointed trustees, so the
receivership was terminated; however, by the end of March 2024, the District had again failed to
maintain a quorum as all trustees had resigned. The Town requested that the Commission again appoint
a receiver. The Commission then travelled to New Sharon for an evidentiary hearing concerning the
need for a receiver and also held a public witness hearing regarding an anticipated rate increase and the
request of the Town for the appointment of a second receiver. As the Commission continued the search
for a receiver, the board was reconstituted by July 1, 2024.
As illustrated, it will likely be in the best interest of the ratepayers for the Town to assume operations
of the District. The issues with finding people willing to be a trustee for the District impacts its
operations and the Town will likely be better equipped to continuously manage the District.
The Commission notes that the language in LD 1346 does not include language regarding the approval
of the transfer by the Commission and this language has been included in other bills effectuating such a transfer. This language is not intended to prevent the transfer but rather is intended to ensure that any transfer is otherwise consistent with all requirements of a regulated utility under Title 35-A.
I would be happy to answer any questions or provide additional information for the work session.

April 15, 2025
Dear Senators and Representatives of the Energy, Utility, and Technology Legislative Committee,
My name is Ed F erreira, and I am a resident of New Sharon and a Trustee of the New Sharon Water District. I am also a homeowner who gets their water from the New Sharon Water District.
I am submitting testimony today to you in support of the bill entitled, "An Act Regarding the Supply of Water to the town of New Sharon," that transfers assets and obligations of the New Sharon Water District to the Town of New Sharon. Currently, the New Sharon Water District is governed by a
charter that was established decades ago which designates that an elected group of trustees oversees
and administrates the water system, the New Sharon Water District. There are approximately 100
users of water on the system and there are approximately 12 water hydrants.
For over a year now, there have been conversations between the New Sharon Water District Trustees and the Select people of the Town of New Sharon. These conversations have been supported by folks
from the Maine Rural Water Association who have assisted us trustees in getting our financial situation stabilized. In the past year there were some loan payment obligations that proved difficult to meet. Those obligations were met and the Water District increased it's monthly user fees by 64% which has
put the water district/system in a more financially sustainable position. In our conversations the Trustees and the Select People have agreed that it would be in the best
interests of both the New Sharon Water District and for the Town of New Sharon for the Town of New
Sharon to assume the assets, operation and administrative responsibility for the public water system in
the town.
There a number of reasons we feel that this is the right way to go. A primary reason is that it would be
administratively efficient. There could be a cost savings of about $13,000 a year in billing costs if the town became the operator of the water system. Another reason is that the system serves a very important function for the town and the town's volunteer fire department by providing a fire hydrant system throughout it's water pipe run. This hydrant system is critical to the mission of the fre
department and helps control the cost of home owner's insurance for all residents of New Sharon. In our view it would make sense for the Town of New Sharon through it's Select People and town
meeting to be the responsible entity for the water system since it serves such a vital role for the entire
town.
The water system is funded by the monthly rates paid for the users of the water, and by an allotment voted on at annual town meeting for fire department's hydrants. Operation and maintenance of the
water system is overseen by our operator Mark Deden and we are not envisioning any major change in the way funding, operation and maintenance are conducted, other than billing and accounting as mentioned earlier, as we currently have sustainable financing, and competent and dedicated water
system operation and personnel. Thank you,
Ed Ferreira
New Sharon Water District Trustee

LD 1346, "An Act Regarding the Supply of Water to the Town of New Sharon"
Joint Standing Committee on Energy Utilities and Technology
April 16, 2025

Senator Lawrence, Representative Sachs, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Energy Utilities and Technology:
My name is Russell Black, and I represent Senate District 5. I'm here to present LD 1346, "An Act Regarding the Supply of Water to the Town of New Sharon."
This bill is a response to an ongoing challenge in the Town. For a while now, the New
Sharon Water District has struggled to maintain a full and functioning board of trustees. That lack of stability has made it difficult to manage the district and provide the level of
service that residents deserve.
LD 1346 proposes to dissolve the water district and transfer its assets, debts, and responsibilities to the Town of New Sharon; but I want to be very clear: this is not a loss
of local control--it is a reinforcement of it. The Town already has the administrative
capacity to oversee water services and is prepared to step in to ensure consistent, accountable management moving forward.
This decision doesn't rest with the Legislature alone. The bill requires a local
referendum, giving the voters of New Sharon the final say. This solution was developed
by the people most directly involved: the current district trustees and the members of the
New Sharon Select Board. They agree this transition is the best path forward, and they're
asking for our help to make it possible,
This bill provides a thoughtful and locally-driven response to a structural issue, and it
ensures that water service in New Sharon remains reliable and responsive to the needs of
the community.
You will hear more from members of the rural water authority and residents of New
Sharon with additional information regarding this bill.
Thank you for your time and consideration.
